## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.

### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)

`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:

- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
  area's allow-list**. A single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
  claimed yet) resolves to `e2e_scope: skip` instead — `e2e-localhost` does not run at all on
  that PR (changed 2026-08-25, at the developer's request; previously fell back to running the
  full suite on every such PR). `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact
  path lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
- **This is a deliberate coverage trade-off, not a gap to silently work around.** A
  `develop`-targeted PR that can't be scoped to one area gets no PR-time E2E run at all — only
  unit tests / Storybook, plus BrowserStack if the PR references a Jira key with a tagged spec.
  Full/non-P0 regression coverage for that PR is deferred to the existing post-merge P0 gates
  (`deploy-test.yml`'s Test-tier gate, `digital-sit.yml`'s `playwright-p0` on `release/**`) —
  which only cover P0-tagged journeys, a subset of the full suite. A non-P0 regression introduced
  by a shared/global-path change can therefore reach `develop` before anything catches it. This
  was accepted deliberately to stop the full suite running on every PR touching a shared path
  (the single largest line item in this repo's CI-minutes usage) — revisit if it causes real
  regressions to slip through in practice.
- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff, unchanged — a release
  PR aggregates a whole sprint and gets the supervised, thorough pre-merge treatment per
  [releaseBranchesRules.md](../../.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md). This skip-instead-of-full
  behavior only applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage silently — it just means that
  spec's PRs get `e2e_scope: skip` (no PR-time run) instead of the scoping optimisation, same as
  any other unclaimed path.

### BrowserStack story scoping

`e2e-browserstack` is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a general regression gate — that's
what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for. It's split across **two** workflows, by
target branch (2026-08-25 cost review — see "What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against"
below for why):

- **`.github/workflows/qa.yml`** — `release/**` PRs. Runs inline alongside the rest of `QA`,
  full suite, unscoped, always against the static `test` tier (no per-branch preview exists for
  a `release/**`/`fix/release-*` branch — see below).
- **`.github/workflows/e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`** — `develop`-targeted PRs. A separate,
  `workflow_run`-triggered workflow, event-driven off `deploy-preview.yml`'s completion (see
  below for why it isn't just another `qa.yml` job).

Both name their one job identically (`Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`), which
`zephyr-results-sync.yml` relies on below.

**How results actually reach Zephyr (SFCC-751).** BrowserStack's own native Jira/Zephyr
integration cannot do this — it only supports US/EU Zephyr API regions, and this org's Zephyr
Scale instance is DE-hosted (confirmed via BrowserStack's Quality Engineering Insights setup
flow, which has no field for a custom Zephyr API host). Instead, `.github/workflows/zephyr-
results-sync.yml` runs after every completed run of **either** `QA` or `Cross-browser E2E
(BrowserStack Preview)` (`workflow_run` watches both): it reads that run's BrowserStack build via
the Test Observability API (`GET /ext/v1/builds/{id}/testRuns` — the one endpoint with a real
per-test `tags` field; classic Automate's `builds.json`/`sessions.json` has none), and for every
result tagged `@zephyr:KEY` (see [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md)), posts a
Pass/Fail execution to Zephyr. On failure, it also files a Jira defect against the `@SFCC-NNN`
story directly via Jira's API — BrowserStack's own "Report a bug" flow is manual-UI-only,
confirmed no CLI/API/MCP path exists for automatic-on-failure filing. Zephyr's REST API has no
attachment endpoint at all (confirmed via multiple SmartBear community threads), so failure
evidence (BrowserStack session link, error text) goes on the Jira defect, not the Zephyr
execution. See `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs`'s doc comment for the full mechanism.

**Both `zephyr-results-sync.yml` and `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` only exist once merged.**
GitHub only evaluates a `workflow_run`-triggering workflow's own definition from the repository's
**default branch** — a copy of either file sitting only on a feature/PR branch is invisible to
GitHub Actions entirely (doesn't even appear in `gh workflow list`) and will never fire, no matter
what happens on that PR. This also means neither workflow can be tested end-to-end against a real
PR before that PR merges — plan around this rather than expect a pre-merge dry run of the trigger
itself (each workflow's underlying *script*/*steps* logic can still be exercised independently —
`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` locally against a real BrowserStack build,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s BrowserStack run itself via `npm run test:story` — just not the
`workflow_run` trigger). `zephyr-results-sync.yml` deliberately does **not** check out
`github.event.workflow_run.head_sha` — a `workflow_run` job carries real secrets regardless of who
triggered the original run, so checking out and executing a PR branch's own version of
`scripts/*.mjs` at that ref would let a modified script on the branch exfiltrate credentials
directly. It checks out the default branch instead (no `ref:` override), which costs nothing given
the above. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` **does** check out the triggering run's `head_sha` — it
has to, to run that PR's own `e2e/tests/zimm` specs and `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` — which
carries the same secrets-alongside-PR-code shape `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack` job already had on
`pull_request`; acceptable only because this repo's branches are always same-repo, never a fork
(see [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules) — revisit if that ever changes.

**Build naming.** `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName`/`testObservabilityOptions.buildName` are both
derived from the PR's primary Jira key via `scripts/computeBuildName.mjs` (`node
scripts/computeBuildName.mjs SFCC-751` → `3-SFCC-751-SFCC-T285 - <short summary>`, prefixed with
`Sprint-` by the yml template) — a live Jira lookup for the sprint number + issue summary, plus a
grep across `e2e/tests/zimm` for any `@zephyr:` tag on a spec also carrying that Jira key. Only
the `develop`-PR path (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`) calls this script with a real key —
`qa.yml`'s `release/**` path has no single primary story, so it just uses the plain run number.
Either job uploads the resulting name as a build artifact; `zephyr-results-sync.yml` downloads
that artifact (via `actions/download-artifact` and the triggering run's ID) instead of
recomputing the name itself — it deliberately checks out `develop`, not the PR branch (see the
workflow's own comment), so an independent recompute there would see a different
`e2e/tests/zimm` spec-file set than the triggering job did whenever a PR adds or renames a
Zephyr-tagged spec, and miss the build lookup entirely until the PR merges. An earlier version of
this paragraph described that as a small, accepted drift risk from calling the script
independently in both jobs — corrected 2026-08-25 (CodeRabbit, PR #61): the risk was real and
guaranteed for exactly this kind of PR, not rare, so it's fixed via artifact-passing instead of
documented as accepted. The download failing is only treated as "nothing to sync" when
`e2e-browserstack` never ran for that triggering run at all (checked via the Actions API); if that
job DID run and the artifact is still missing, the sync job fails loudly instead of guessing a
fallback name that could silently miss a real BrowserStack build (CodeRabbit flagged this
correctly, 2026-08-25).

**Desktop/mobile project isolation — a real gotcha, not a style choice.** BrowserStack Test
Observability groups results by test *title* across what it calls "reruns," regardless of which
Playwright project produced them. A spec whose desktop assertions pass on `chromium` and whose
mobile assertions are skipped or fail on `mobile-chrome` — if both share one test title — collapses
to a single dashboard row showing only the *last-recorded* status, silently hiding whichever
result didn't "win" (confirmed against real build data, SFCC-751, 2026-08-25 — a build with 11
real chromium passes and 11 skipped mobile-chrome entries under identical titles showed
`passed: 0, skipped: 11` via BrowserStack's own API, not just the dashboard UI). `test.skip()`
does not avoid this — the skipped entry still shares the title and still clobbers.

The only real fix is to stop the "wrong" project from ever collecting that test at all, which
`playwright.config.js`'s existing per-project `testIgnore` already supports: the `chromium`
project ignores `**/mobile/**`, and `mobile-chrome` ignores `**/desktop/**`. When a spec has
platform-specific assertions that would otherwise share a title across projects, split it into
genuinely separate files under sibling `desktop/`/`mobile/` folders (e.g.
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/desktop/SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js` and
`e2e/tests/zimm/homepage/mobile/SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js`) rather than one file with
per-project `test.skip()` branches — that keeps each test's title unique to the one project that
ever runs it for real, so pass/fail on one project can never be overwritten by a skip or a
different result from the other. Same-file-with-distinct-titles was tried and rejected for this
exact reason — the underlying `test()` call is still collected (and skipped) on the other project
regardless of what its title says.

**Access-gated preview URLs.** `BasePage.goto()` supports two optional env vars,
`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE`, for a `RETAIL_APP_HOME` that requires a custom
header to reach at all (e.g. an access-gated MRT preview URL) — unset by default, so SIT/
production targets need neither. Not Didomi-specific; a generic single header pair, since that's
the one real case this repo has needed so far.

**What `e2e-browserstack` actually tests against.** Not the static `test` tier by default —
`test` only updates via deliberate tag promotion (see [tagging.md](./tagging.md)), so its
currently-deployed build has no guaranteed relationship to any given PR. On the `develop`-PR path,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` downloads the hostname `deploy-preview.yml` persisted as an
artifact on its own run (ephemeral `pr-<slug>` MRT target, deployed on every push to the branch —
see that workflow) and points BrowserStack there — so it's testing this PR's own code.

**No fallback to the static test tier when that artifact is missing (removed 2026-08-26,
CodeRabbit flagged this correctly)** — an earlier version of this job silently fell back to the
static `test`-tier `RETAIL_APP_HOME` whenever `deploy-preview.yml` failed or hadn't finished. That
let a develop PR whose own deployment genuinely failed still produce a green, story-tagged Zephyr
execution (and a possible auto-filed Jira defect) that proved nothing about the PR's own code —
the exact condition the fallback existed to tolerate was the one that made its result meaningless.
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s "Resolve BrowserStack test target" step now fails the job loudly
(`::error::` + `exit 1`) instead when the hostname artifact is missing, whether that's because
Deploy Preview failed outright or succeeded but didn't reach the artifact-upload step. Same
principle [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md)'s Graceful Degradation section already states for
checkout/payment: never silently substitute a different flow, surface an explicit error instead.
A cancelled Deploy Preview run is the one case with nothing to fail loudly about — the job-level
`if:` skips the whole job entirely rather than running it just to hit this failure, since there's
no meaningful error to surface for a run nobody asked to complete.

**This used to be a single job in `qa.yml` that polled for `deploy-preview.yml`'s run to finish —
that design is gone, not just retuned (2026-08-25 cost review).** It started alongside `Deploy
Preview` (both triggered by the same push) and slept in a loop waiting for it, since there was no
other way for one already-running, already-billed job to wait on a *different* workflow's run —
up to ~17 minutes of pure idle runner time per push, worst case, before the real BrowserStack run
even started. (An earlier version of this note described tuning that wait down from a wrongly
inflated 70-minute job timeout / 40-minute poll to 40/15 — that tuning is now moot; the wait
itself no longer exists.) `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml` fixes this at the root by being a
separate workflow, `workflow_run`-triggered off `Deploy Preview`'s completion: GitHub fires it
the instant that run finishes, with the run ID and conclusion already in the event payload — no
polling, so no billed wait, ever. `release/**` PRs were never part of this problem —
`deploy-preview.yml` never runs for `fix/release-*` branches, so `qa.yml`'s `e2e-browserstack`
job (which still handles that path) goes straight to the static test tier with nothing to wait
for.

- **`release/**`-targeted PRs (`qa.yml`):** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped.
  A release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
- **`develop`-targeted PRs (`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`):** on `Deploy Preview`'s completion,
  the job finds the open PR for that branch (`gh pr list --head`, one call, no loop) and regexes
  `SFCC-\d+` out of its title, body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app
  uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own (duplicated from
  `qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` step rather than shared — the two workflows have no other runtime
  dependency on each other). If at least one key is found, the job runs `--grep`-scoped to that
  story's tag(s) (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job exits
  without running BrowserStack.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results
  to in Zephyr, there's nothing correct to run. It also re-checks `qa.yml`'s own `e2e`-path
  relevance gate before running — a single non-looping artifact download from that commit's `QA`
  run — **but this is a fail-open check, not an unconditional guarantee** (CodeRabbit flagged the
  distinction correctly, 2026-08-26): the normal path is that a Jira-tagged PR touching nothing
  e2e-relevant genuinely skips BrowserStack. If the QA-run lookup or the `e2e-scope` artifact
  download itself fails for any reason (the run isn't found yet, the artifact expired, an API
  hiccup), this step assumes relevant rather than adding a retry loop to chase the optimisation —
  so in that specific failure case, a Jira-tagged PR can still run BrowserStack even when its
  changes weren't e2e-relevant. Worst case is one avoidable BrowserStack run, not a correctness
  problem, but it's a real exception to the "doesn't pay for a BrowserStack run" claim, not a
  universal guarantee.
- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
  by `e2e-localhost`.
- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:


**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see
[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

# TypeScript Conventions

TypeScript-specific idioms that apply to every `.ts`/`.tsx` file. See
[conventions.md](./conventions.md) for the base "TypeScript only inside `overrides/`" rule
and general cross-cutting conventions; see [components.md](./components.md) for how these
apply specifically to component props and hook signatures.

---

- **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible.
  Prefer `unknown` with a type guard when the shape is genuinely not known at that point.
- **Prefer `type` over `interface`** for component props, shared shapes, and utility type
  aliases. Use `interface` only when declaration merging is genuinely needed.
- **No non-null assertion (`!`)** without an inline comment explaining why the value is
  guaranteed non-null at that point — same reasoning as the `any` policy. Prefer a proper
  null check, an early return, or narrowing the type instead.
- **Discriminated unions for variant/state modeling.** When a value can be one of several
  distinct shapes (e.g. a basket item that's either a product or a gift card, or a fetch
  state that's loading/error/success), model it as a discriminated union with a common
  literal `kind`/`type` field rather than one type with a pile of optional fields. Lets
  TypeScript narrow correctly in each branch instead of requiring manual `? :` guards.
- **Prefer utility types over hand-rolled duplicate shapes.** `Pick<ProductTileProps, 'id' | 'name'>`,
  `Omit<...>`, `Partial<...>`, `Required<...>` — reach for these before redeclaring a
  near-identical type by hand. A hand-copied type silently drifts from its source when the
  original changes; a utility type doesn't.
- **`import type` for type-only imports.** `import type {ProductTileProps} from './types'` —
  keeps type-only imports from ending up in the compiled bundle and makes the type-vs-value
  distinction explicit at the import site.
- **`satisfies` over a type assertion (`as`)** when you want literal-type inference _and_
  a check that the value conforms to a type — e.g. a config object where you want
  autocomplete on the literal keys but also compiler validation against a shape. Reach for
  `as` only when you're genuinely overriding what TypeScript can infer (and treat that the
  same as an `any` — comment why).
- **`readonly`** on props and arrays that the receiving component/function must not mutate
  — particularly array/object props passed down from a parent that still owns that data.
  Signals intent at the type level instead of relying on convention alone.
- **Generic type parameter naming.** Single-letter (`T`, `K`, `V`) is fine for a generic
  utility with one obvious parameter. Once there's more than one type parameter, or the
  generic's role isn't obvious from context, use a descriptive name prefixed with `T`
  (`TItem`, `TResponse`) so the signature reads clearly without having to trace usage.

4

6

8	  /** Whether the drawer is open. */
9	  isOpen: boolean;
10	  /** Called on backdrop click, Escape, and the close button (all via ZimmDrawer/Chakra's Drawer). */
11	  onClose: () => void;
12	  /** Number of line items in the bag. Drives the header title only ("BAG • {itemCount}" vs
13	   *  "YOUR BAG IS EMPTY") — see `children`'s own doc below for the empty-vs-populated body. */
14	  itemCount: number;
15	  /** Element to focus once the drawer finishes closing — see ZimmDrawer's own doc (AC10
16	   *  focus-return); without this Chakra falls back to focusing document.body. */
17	  finalFocusRef?: React.RefObject<HTMLElement>;
18	  /** Cart line items — or the empty-state body. This organism owns no item-rendering logic and
19	   *  no empty-vs-populated decision itself: it renders whatever `children` it is given,
20	   *  unconditionally, regardless of `itemCount`. The caller (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, SFCC-11
21	   *  plan step 4.6) decides between the real item list and `ZimmCartEmptyState`. */
22	  children: React.ReactNode;
23	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-404's message-aggregation system (validation/error/promo banners).
24	   *  Always rendered, even with nothing passed — see zimmCartDrawer.css.ts's `messages` part:
25	   *  the band reserves height regardless, so the drawer doesn't change position when a message
26	   *  appears or disappears. */
27	  messages?: React.ReactNode;
28	  /** Reserved slot for SFCC-275's button group (checkout / continue shopping). Not built in this
29	   *  commit (SFCC-315 is shell-only) — this organism only provides the slot it will render into
30	   *  later. */
31	  footer?: React.ReactNode;
32	};
33	
34	/**
35	 * SFCC-315 — the Cart drawer shell. Wraps ZimmDrawer (size="xLarge") with the cart-specific
36	 * header title, a height-reserving messages band, a responsive items/totals layout, and a
37	 * footer slot.
38	 *
39	 * Deliberately not wired to a trigger yet — no `_app`/`product-view` changes, no
40	 * `useCartDrawer` hook, no button-group content, no message aggregation. Those remain separate,
41	 * later commits in this same plan — this organism is exercised only via its own Storybook
42	 * stories today. (Corrected 2026-09-21, SFCC-11 plan step 4.6: this paragraph used to also list
43	 * "no real empty-state body" here — no longer true. This component itself never owned that
44	 * decision; it renders whatever `children` it is given unconditionally. The real empty-state
45	 * body — deciding between the item list and `ZimmCartEmptyState` — is `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`'s
46	 * job, per `ZimmCartDrawerProps.children`'s own doc above.)
47	 *
48	 * Figma-fidelity audit fix, 2026-09-19: `ZimmDrawer`'s `title` was passed with no `titleStyle`,
49	 * so it silently took that prop's default (`'large'` → `heading1`, 24px) instead of the Figma
50	 * spec for this header ("BAG • #", 14px medium — `body2Strong`). Measured live before the fix:
51	 * 24px/400/32px against the 14px/500 spec. `ZimmDrawer` itself already supports both correctly
52	 * (`titleStyle="small"` → `body2Strong`, confirmed against `typography.ts`) — this was a missing
53	 * prop at the call site, not a defect in `ZimmDrawer`.
54	 *
55	 * @param props see ZimmCartDrawerProps
56	 */
57	export const ZimmCartDrawer = ({
58	  isOpen,
59	  onClose,
60	  itemCount,
61	  finalFocusRef,
62	  children,
63	  messages,
64	  footer,
65	}: ZimmCartDrawerProps) => {
66	  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_CART_DRAWER_RECIPE, {});
67	  const title = itemCount === 0 ? 'YOUR BAG IS EMPTY' : `BAG • ${itemCount}`;
68	
69	  return (
70	    <ZimmDrawer
71	      isOpen={isOpen}
72	      onClose={onClose}
73	      size="xLarge"
74	      title={title}
75	      titleStyle="small"
76	      finalFocusRef={finalFocusRef}
77	    >
78	      <chakra.div __css={styles.messages}>{messages}</chakra.div>
79	      {/* SFCC-11 plan step 4.6 fix: this used to be `itemCount === 0 ? <hardcoded placeholder> :
80	          children` — ignoring `children` entirely at zero items, no matter what the caller passed.
81	          Renders `children` unconditionally now; the empty-vs-populated decision belongs entirely
82	          to the caller (see ZimmCartDrawerProps.children's own doc above). */}
83	      <chakra.div __css={styles.body}>{children}</chakra.div>
84	      <chakra.div __css={styles.footer}>{footer}</chakra.div>
85	    </ZimmDrawer>
86	  );
87	};

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option); the `model` parameter here overrides the definition for this one call.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative — "will I need this output again" — not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this — it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path — do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running — give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* — what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.


## Writing the prompt

Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

For fresh agents, terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

Example usage:

<example>
user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this — it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>
Agent({
  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn — the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
<commentary>
A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.
</commentary>
Agent({
  name: "migration-review",
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes — I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
</example>

user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"

  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",

assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.

2	import { findImageGroupBy } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/image-groups-utils';
3	import { getDisplayVariationValues } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
4	
5	/*
6	 * Converts an SDK basket `productItem` into a self-contained display-data shape, mirroring the
7	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` precedent (`overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`,
8	 * PR #85) for how a page-scoped SDK-to-props mapper is organised in this codebase: exported
9	 * "select"-prefixed functions (that file exports three: `selectGalleryImages`,
10	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, `selectProductListCard` - corrected here, an earlier draft of this
11	 * comment said "a single" one, which was wrong), an untyped-base-package input narrowed to a
12	 * local type, and a `.test.ts` asserting the mapped shape directly (see that file's own
13	 * `ProductListSearchHit`/`RawImage` pattern, mirrored below for `CartLineItem`/`CartItemImage`).
14	 *
15	 * Disclosed design choice, not a directly sourced requirement (flagged per this step's own
16	 * instructions): `ProductItem`/`ItemVariantProvider` (`overrides/app/components/product-item/
17	 * index.tsx:140`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/index.tsx:43`) both currently declare
18	 * their real data-carrying prop as the raw untyped basket/product object itself
19	 * (`product`/`variant`, both `SfccProduct`/`SfccVariant = any`) — today's leaves read every
20	 * display field (image, name, combined attributes) directly off that object via
21	 * `useItemVariant()`, not from individually-mapped props. This mapper is, per this step's plan
22	 * text, "an as-yet-unused-by-anything-else container-layer function" — it does not change or
23	 * feed either of those two files (out of this step's scope). What it produces instead is a pure,
24	 * tested equivalent of the specific per-field computations those leaves and
25	 * `product-quantity-picker.tsx`/`use-derived-product.js` already perform internally off that same
26	 * raw object (image+alt, combined colour/size, quantity, stepQuantity) — ready for whichever
27	 * future step decides how a real page hands data down, without having modified any of those
28	 * existing files.
29	 *
30	 * `CartLineItem` models the REAL runtime shape a basket line item has by the time it reaches
31	 * those leaves: the un-overridden base cart page never passes the raw `basket.productItems[i]`
32	 * alone — it merges it with the matching full `Product` (fetched separately via `useProducts`)
33	 * before handing it down: `product={{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[productItem.itemId],
34	 * price: productItem.price, quantity: ...}}` (see
35	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-item-list/index.jsx`, the
36	 * `<ProductItem product={...}>` call). `imageGroups`/`variationAttributes`/`variationValues`/
37	 * `stepQuantity`/`name` all come from that merged-in `Product` half, not from
38	 * `ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem` itself (confirmed against its generated fields — it has no
39	 * image/variation/stepQuantity fields at all beyond its own `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all).
40	 *
41	 * Both halves are `Pick`'d, not intersected raw (zm-tester, SFCC-11 step 3.4 finding): the real
42	 * generated `ProductItem` type carries the identical `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all the comment
43	 * above already calls out on `Product`. Intersecting it raw would silently resolve a typo'd field
44	 * name (or a nonexistent one) to `any` instead of a compile error — empirically confirmed harmless
45	 * today (every real access below is spelled correctly) but a real, latent gap a future edit could
46	 * hit silently. `Pick`ing both halves closes it the same way on both sides.
47	 */
48	type CartLineItem = Pick<ShopperBasketsTypes.ProductItem, 'itemId' | 'productId' | 'quantity' | 'productName'> &
49	  Pick<
50	    ShopperProductsTypes.Product,
51	    'imageGroups' | 'variationAttributes' | 'variationValues' | 'stepQuantity' | 'name'
52	  >;
53	
54	type CartItemImage = {
55	  src?: string;
56	  /**
57	   * Always a string, never undefined — even when there's no image at all (falls back to the
58	   * item's own name, then `''`). See `selectCartItemImage`'s own doc comment for the fallback
59	   * chain and why this differs from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns
60	   * `undefined` for the whole image on a miss instead.
61	   */
62	  alt: string;
63	};
64	
65	type CartItemMapperResult = {
66	  itemId?: string;
67	  productId?: string;
68	  name: string;
69	  image: CartItemImage;
70	  combinedAttributes: string;
71	  quantity?: number;
72	  stepQuantity: number;
73	};
74	
75	/**
76	 * Matches `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-derived-product.js:38`'s own
77	 * `product?.stepQuantity || 1` exactly — reused as a value, not a shared import, since that hook
78	 * itself isn't a pure function this module can call (it's stateful, `useState`-backed).
79	 */
80	const DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY = 1;
81	
82	/**
83	 * Selects this line item's display image, always returning a defined `alt` even when there is no
84	 * image at all (unlike `productListCardMapper.ts`'s `toCardImage`, which returns `undefined` for
85	 * the whole image on a miss — a PLP card can legitimately skip rendering entirely when it has
86	 * nothing to show; a cart line item cannot, per this step's own pass criteria).
87	 *
88	 * The lookup itself reuses `findImageGroupBy` exactly as
89	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-image.tsx:70-73` already does (same `viewType:
90	 * 'small'` / `selectedVariationAttributes` call) rather than reimplementing image-group matching.
91	 */
92	const selectCartItemImage = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemImage => {
93	  const image = findImageGroupBy(item.imageGroups, {
94	    viewType: 'small',
95	    selectedVariationAttributes: item.variationValues,
96	  })?.images?.[0];
97	
98	  return {
99	    src: image?.disBaseLink || image?.link,
100	    alt: image?.alt || item.productName || item.name || '',
101	  };
102	};
103	
104	/**
105	 * Combines the colour and size variation values into the single string the Figma cart-item spec
106	 * calls for, reusing the exact mechanism
107	 * `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-attributes.tsx:98,148-150` already uses for its own
108	 * `combineAttributeValues` behaviour (`getDisplayVariationValues(...)` then
109	 * `Object.values(...).join(', ')`) rather than reimplementing string-combining from scratch.
110	 *
111	 * Ordering is inherited from that same call, not independently re-sorted here: it reflects
112	 * whichever order the incoming `variationValues` object's own keys are in (see
113	 * `getDisplayVariationValues`'s `Object.entries(values).reduce(...)`,
114	 * `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:30`). This is the
115	 * identical mechanism `item-attributes.tsx`'s own docblock (line 31) already cites as producing
116	 * "Lilac Sand, One size" (colour, size) for real Zimmermann catalog data —
117	 * `product-item/index.tsx`'s docblock (line 44) corroborates the same combined-string behaviour
118	 * generically ("colour, size") without repeating that specific example. This function inherits
119	 * that already-verified behaviour rather than re-guaranteeing the order independently.
120	 */
121	const selectCombinedAttributes = (item: CartLineItem): string => {
122	  const variationValues = getDisplayVariationValues(item.variationAttributes, item.variationValues);
123	  return variationValues ? Object.values(variationValues).join(', ') : '';
124	};
125	
126	/**
127	 * Maps one basket line item (already merged with its full product data — see this file's own
128	 * module docblock) to a plain display-data shape: image, name, one combined colour/size string,
129	 * and quantity/stepQuantity passed through. Pure function, no hooks — keeps every consumer in B3
130	 * prop-driven with no data-fetching hook in a leaf, per this step's own plan text.
131	 */
132	export const selectCartItemProps = (item: CartLineItem): CartItemMapperResult => ({
133	  itemId: item.itemId,
134	  productId: item.productId,
135	  name: item.productName || item.name || '',
136	  image: selectCartItemImage(item),
137	  combinedAttributes: selectCombinedAttributes(item),
138	  quantity: item.quantity,
139	  stepQuantity: item.stepQuantity || DEFAULT_STEP_QUANTITY,
140	});

1	import { useQueryClient } from '@tanstack/react-query';
2	import type { ShopperBasketsV2Types } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
3	import { useShopperBasketsV2Mutation as useShopperBasketsMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
4	import { getMaxOrderQuantity } from 'app/utils/maxOrderQuantity';
5	
6	/**
7	 * The minimal basket shape this hook needs, regardless of which caller supplies it: the
8	 * post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`, wired in this step) passes the resolved value
9	 * of its own `mergeBasket` mutation directly; the cart drawer's render guard
10	 * (`overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, step 4.6 — not yet built) will pass its
11	 * own `useCurrentBasket()` data. `Pick`-narrowed, matching `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own established
12	 * pattern for taking an untyped-at-the-edges SDK response and narrowing it to only the fields a
13	 * pure function actually reads, rather than depending on the exact generic SDK response type
14	 * either caller's own mutation/query hook happens to produce.
15	 */
16	export type CartCapBasket = Pick<ShopperBasketsV2Types.Basket, 'basketId' | 'lastModified' | 'productItems'>;
17	
18	/**
19	 * Outcome of one `capBasketQuantities` call. A discriminated union (typescript.md's guidance for
20	 * variant/state modelling) rather than a boolean-plus-optional-error: each branch is something a
21	 * caller could reasonably want to react to differently, and no AC or copy exists yet for any of
22	 * them (that is `useCartMessages`, step 4.3, not built) — this file only reports what happened,
23	 * it does not decide what the shopper sees.
24	 */
25	export type CartCapResult =
26	  | { status: 'not-needed' }
27	  | { status: 'skipped'; reason: 'mutation-in-flight' | 'already-attempted-this-version' }
28	  | { status: 'corrected' }
29	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
30	
31	/**
32	 * `getMaxOrderQuantity` is typed for a SCAPI product response (`id: string` required — see
33	 * `overrides/app/utils/maxOrderQuantity.ts`). A basket line item has no `id` field at all: only
34	 * `itemId`/`productId` (confirmed against the generated `BasketProductItem` type — verified via
35	 * a throwaway `tsc` repro that assigning a same-shaped object to a type requiring `id` fails
36	 * with "Property 'id' is missing"), so passing one directly does not type-check, despite it
37	 * carrying the same `{[key: string]: any}` catch-all a real `c_maxOrderQuantity` value would
38	 * arrive through once SFCC-268 ships. `product-item/index.tsx` already lives with the identical
39	 * gap at its own `getMaxOrderQuantity(product)` call site (`type SfccProduct = any`, lines 171
40	 * and 331) — narrowed here with an explicit, commented cast instead of a bare `any` parameter,
41	 * per typescript.md's "no `any` without an inline comment" rule.
42	 */
43	const getLineMaxOrderQuantity = (item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem): number =>
44	  getMaxOrderQuantity(item as unknown as Parameters<typeof getMaxOrderQuantity>[0]);
45	
46	/**
47	 * A line needs correction once its quantity exceeds the cap — i.e. once it reaches the smallest
48	 * over-cap value (`max + 1`; `4` when `max` is `3`) or anything above it. Written as `quantity >
49	 * max` rather than comparing against a separately-named `max + 1` boundary, but the two are the
50	 * same comparison: this must be a "the whole range above the boundary" check, not an
51	 * exact-equality check against a single value — an equality check against `max + 1` alone would
52	 * correctly catch a line at 4 but wrongly leave a line at 5 or more uncorrected, which is
53	 * observably wrong against this hook's own test fixture (a line at 5 must reduce to 3, not stay
54	 * at 5).
55	 */
56	const needsQuantityCorrection = (
57	  item: ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem,
58	): item is ShopperBasketsV2Types.BasketProductItem & { quantity: number } =>
59	  typeof item.quantity === 'number' && item.quantity > getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item);
60	
61	/**
62	 * SFCC baskets carry no explicit version counter. `basketId` + `lastModified` change together on
63	 * every write SFCC accepts (both real fields on the generated `Basket` type), so the pair is a
64	 * workable proxy for "the exact basket state a correction was last attempted against" — this is
65	 * this file's own reasoned choice, not sourced from an existing codebase precedent or doc.
66	 */
67	const getBasketVersionKey = (basket: CartCapBasket): string => `${basket.basketId ?? ''}:${basket.lastModified ?? ''}`;
68	
69	/**
70	 * Storage key for "which basket version has a correction already been attempted against."
71	 * Deliberately not a `useRef` — the post-auth callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`) and the
72	 * future render guard (step 4.6) each get their own separate `useCartMergeAndCap()` call, and
73	 * therefore their own separate refs, since they mount in two different React component trees. A
74	 * plain ref cannot coordinate between them. Piggybacking on the already-global `QueryClient` (the
75	 * same one `capBasketQuantities`'s own mutation-in-flight guard reads from — see that function's
76	 * own comment) via `getQueryData`/`setQueryData` gives real cross-instance-shared storage without
77	 * inventing a new module-level singleton or Context provider. It is also, unlike a React-render-
78	 * time hook value, live/imperative — reading and then
79	 * immediately writing it inside `capBasketQuantities` with no `await` in between (see that
80	 * function) leaves no window for two near-simultaneous calls to both pass the check before either
81	 * has recorded its attempt, since JavaScript runs that synchronous read-then-write as one
82	 * uninterruptible step.
83	 */
84	const CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY = ['zimmCartMergeAndCap', 'attemptedBasketVersion'] as const;
85	
86	export type UseCartMergeAndCapReturn = {
87	  /**
88	   * Checks every basket line against `getMaxOrderQuantity` and, if any line exceeds its cap,
89	   * issues one `updateItemsInBasket` write reducing every over-cap line to its own max in a
90	   * single request (matching the SFCC-11 plan's "one write" framing even when more than one line
91	   * needs correcting). Resolves only once that write — if one was issued — has fully settled, so
92	   * a caller sequencing merge -> cap -> a future wishlist-resume can `await` this in turn without
93	   * racing it.
94	   */
95	  capBasketQuantities: (basket: CartCapBasket) => Promise<CartCapResult>;
96	};
97	
98	/**
99	 * Hook — the shared "cap" half of SFCC-250's merge-then-cap flow. Two callers share this one
100	 * implementation, not two copies: the post-auth callback inside `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own
101	 * `isRegistered` effect (wired in this step, right after that effect's existing `mergeBasket`
102	 * call), and the cart drawer's render guard, which will live in
103	 * `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (not yet built — a later step, 4.6, wires
104	 * that second call site; this hook is written to support it, not to assume it already exists).
105	 *
106	 * Per rules-of-hooks, call this at the top level of whichever hook or component needs it — never
107	 * from inside a `useEffect` callback — and invoke the returned `capBasketQuantities` function
108	 * itself from inside the effect/render path instead.
109	 *
110	 * @returns `capBasketQuantities`, the one function both callers invoke.
111	 */
112	export const useCartMergeAndCap = (): UseCartMergeAndCapReturn => {
113	  const queryClient = useQueryClient();
114	  const updateItemsInBasket = useShopperBasketsMutation('updateItemsInBasket');
115	
116	  const capBasketQuantities = async (basket: CartCapBasket): Promise<CartCapResult> => {
117	    // No-op while any mutation is in flight (this hook's own prior correction, the merge that
118	    // just ran, a shopper's manual quantity edit — anything) so this can never race a write
119	    // already under way. See this function's own JSDoc.
120	    //
121	    // REWORK (round 1, Tester-confirmed defect): this must be a LIVE read taken at the moment
122	    // this function actually runs — not a React-render-time value closed over at this hook's own
123	    // top level. `capBasketQuantities` is captured once by its caller and invoked later, from
124	    // inside an async callback (`useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s `mergeBasket.mutate(...).onSuccess`,
125	    // itself only reachable after a real network round trip) with no guarantee that hook instance
126	    // re-renders in between. A `useIsMutating()` value read at this hook's own top level (the
127	    // original approach here) would still reflect whatever mutation count existed at that earlier
128	    // render, not the real state at the moment this guard actually needs to check it.
129	    //
130	    // `queryClient.isMutating(filters?)` (confirmed against the installed
131	    // `@tanstack/query-core@4.43.0` source — a single deduped version across this project's whole
132	    // dependency tree, per `npm ls @tanstack/react-query` — `node_modules/@tanstack/query-core/
133	    // build/lib/queryClient.esm.js`: `isMutating(filters) { return this.mutationCache.findAll(
134	    // {...filters, fetching: true}).length; }`) computes this fresh from the live mutation cache
135	    // on every call. It is the exact same computation `useIsMutating()` itself wraps in
136	    // `useSyncExternalStore` for React reactivity (`node_modules/@tanstack/react-query/build/lib/
137	    // useIsMutating.esm.js`: `() => queryClient.isMutating(filters)`), just read directly instead
138	    // of through a render-synced subscription — so this preserves the exact same "every mutation
139	    // anywhere in the app" scope this guard has always had (commerce-sdk-react's basket mutation
140	    // hooks set no `mutationKey`, so an unscoped call is still the only reading that sees all of
141	    // them), it now just reads that scope live instead of stale.
142	    if (queryClient.isMutating() > 0) {
143	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'mutation-in-flight' };
144	    }
145	
146	    const correctedItems = (basket.productItems ?? []).filter(needsQuantityCorrection).map((item) => ({
147	      itemId: item.itemId,
148	      productId: item.productId,
149	      quantity: getLineMaxOrderQuantity(item),
150	    }));
151	
152	    if (correctedItems.length === 0) {
153	      return { status: 'not-needed' };
154	    }
155	
156	    if (!basket.basketId) {
157	      // No basketId means there is nothing valid to address a write at — surface this as an
158	      // error rather than silently doing nothing, so a caller can tell "nothing needed fixing"
159	      // apart from "something needed fixing and couldn't be".
160	      return { status: 'error', error: new Error('useCartMergeAndCap: basket is missing a basketId.') };
161	    }
162	
163	    const versionKey = getBasketVersionKey(basket);
164	    if (queryClient.getQueryData<string>(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY) === versionKey) {
165	      // Loop guard: a correction has already been attempted against this exact basket state,
166	      // whether it succeeded or failed — do not retry it. See CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY's own
167	      // comment for why this is a live cache read rather than a per-instance ref, and why
168	      // setting it below, before the `await`, is what keeps this race-free.
169	      return { status: 'skipped', reason: 'already-attempted-this-version' };
170	    }
171	    queryClient.setQueryData(CAP_ATTEMPT_QUERY_KEY, versionKey);
172	
173	    try {
174	      await updateItemsInBasket.mutateAsync({
175	        parameters: { basketId: basket.basketId },
176	        body: correctedItems,
177	      });
178	      return { status: 'corrected' };
179	    } catch (error) {
180	      // Surfaced to the caller, not retried: the version is already marked attempted above, so a
181	      // later call against this same unchanged basket state returns 'skipped' rather than
182	      // hammering the server again — no retry storm.
183	      return { status: 'error', error };
184	    }
185	  };
186	
187	  return { capBasketQuantities };
188	};

1	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
2	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
3	
4	/**
5	 * `@salesforce/retail-react-app` ships no TypeScript types (AGENTS.md's "Commerce SDK types not
6	 * importable" gotcha) — `use-toast.js` falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s catch-all
7	 * `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'` (a shorthand ambient module declaration that
8	 * types the whole module `any` — see that file's own comment, and
9	 * `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts`'s identical narrow-local-type pattern for
10	 * another untyped base function), so the real `useToast()` return value is implicitly `any`.
11	 * Declared narrow here, covering only the two fields this file actually sends (`title`, `status`)
12	 * rather than the base hook's full options surface (`description`, `action`, `position`,
13	 * `duration`, `variant`, `isClosable`) — nothing in this file uses those, so typing them would be
14	 * speculative. `status`'s four values are copied verbatim from the base hook's real accepted set
15	 * (not narrowed to only `'success' | 'warning'`), so a later message that genuinely needs `'error'`
16	 * or `'info'` — SFCC-404's rework, or any message added after this step — is already covered
17	 * without a signature change here.
18	 *
19	 * This is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee — TypeScript
20	 * allows asserting `any` to any narrower type with no check. The real proof is this file's own
21	 * test, which asserts the exact object the mocked toast function is called with.
22	 */
23	type CartToastStatus = 'success' | 'error' | 'info' | 'warning';
24	type CartToastFn = (options: { title: string; status: CartToastStatus }) => void;
25	
26	/**
27	 * The three real cart messages this step ships, copy verbatim from Figma (SFCC-11 plan step 4.3)
28	 * — this file never derives or paraphrases copy, only interpolates a product name into the one
29	 * message that needs it. SFCC-272's own AC text describes a generic stacked wording ("Item added
30	 * to Wishlist") for when more than one item has been added — deliberately not built here: a toast
31	 * has no aggregation concept, so that copy is only reachable once SFCC-404 ships real message
32	 * stacking. Until then every add uses this product-named variant, one toast per add.
33	 *
34	 * Wrapped in `defineMessages` (fixed 2026-09-20 — the original version of this file hardcoded
35	 * plain strings, the only visible cart copy in this build that did) so these three strings are
36	 * discoverable by whatever tooling extracts copy for this storefront's 11 locales the same way
37	 * `zimmQuantityStepper`'s own `messages` object already is. `defaultMessage` uses ICU
38	 * MessageFormat's `{productName}` placeholder syntax for the one message that interpolates.
39	 */
40	const messages = defineMessages({
41	  addedToWishlist: {
42	    id: 'use_cart_messages.added_to_wishlist',
43	    defaultMessage: '{productName} added to Wishlist',
44	  },
45	  alreadyInWishlist: {
46	    id: 'use_cart_messages.already_in_wishlist',
47	    defaultMessage: 'An item in your bag already exists in Wishlist',
48	  },
49	  maxQuantityReached: {
50	    id: 'use_cart_messages.max_quantity_reached',
51	    defaultMessage: 'An item in your bag has reached maximum quantity',
52	  },
53	});
54	
55	export type UseCartMessagesReturn = {
56	  /**
57	   * SFCC-272 AC5 — a single product was moved from the cart to the wishlist. `productName` is
58	   * interpolated into the copy on every call — never hardcode a specific product's name at a call
59	   * site. `success` status.
60	   */
61	  notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) => void;
62	  /**
63	   * SFCC-272 AC6 — the item already exists in the shopper's wishlist; the caller leaves the cart
64	   * line untouched. Verbatim copy, no interpolation. `warning` status — see
65	   * `notifyMaxQuantityReached`'s own doc for why cart feedback that doesn't block anything reads
66	   * as a warning in this build, not an error.
67	   */
68	  notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => void;
69	  /**
70	   * CAI-017 / SFCC-250 — a cart line has reached its maximum orderable quantity (the line is
71	   * already capped by `useCartMergeAndCap` before this ever fires). `warning`, not `error`:
72	   * CAI-017's own requirement text says "an error message will be displayed", but the Figma
73	   * rendering uses the warning variant and SFCC-250 AC4 confirms this never blocks checkout — this
74	   * build's own gate resolved the wording as meaning user-facing feedback, not literally Chakra's
75	   * error severity (the same reconciliation `ZimmInlineMessage`'s own `variant` prop documents —
76	   * `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmInlineMessage/index.tsx`: "a caller may
77	   * legitimately pass `variant=\"warning\"` for copy whose own requirement text uses the word
78	   * `error`").
79	   */
80	  notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => void;
81	};
82	
83	/**
84	 * Hook — the one surface every cart toast message (success and warning today; whatever SFCC-404's
85	 * real stacking/aggregation rework needs later, including a genuine error) is sent through.
86	 * `emitCartMessage` below is the single call to the underlying toast function — a future rework
87	 * swaps what happens inside this one file, not a hunt across the cart UI for every place that
88	 * fires a toast.
89	 *
90	 * Wraps the **base** `useToast` (`@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast`) rather than a
91	 * new `overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts` — that path does not exist, and creating it would be an
92	 * unbudgeted Tier 2 change (`protectedFiles.md` would route it to both squads plus tier-2/tier-1
93	 * approvers). See the SFCC-11 plan's own resolved open question 4. This hook is the real "one
94	 * handler" the plan asks for; the base hook underneath it is just the interim renderer SFCC-404
95	 * replaces.
96	 *
97	 * @returns the three named cart-message senders callers actually invoke today. `emitCartMessage`
98	 * itself is intentionally not returned — nothing outside this file needs to send an
99	 * uncatalogued/arbitrary message yet, and a future message is one new named function here, not a
100	 * reason to widen this hook's public surface.
101	 */
102	export const useCartMessages = (): UseCartMessagesReturn => {
103	  // Real return type is implicit `any` (see CartToastFn's own docblock above) — asserted to the
104	  // local narrow type rather than left as `any`, so every call below is checked against the shape
105	  // this file actually depends on.
106	  const toast = useToast() as CartToastFn;
107	  const intl = useIntl();
108	
109	  const emitCartMessage = (title: string, status: CartToastStatus): void => {
110	    // SFCC-404: this is the one real call to the underlying toast function. When SFCC-404's real
111	    // stacking/aggregation rework lands, this is the only line that changes.
112	    toast({ title, status });
113	  };
114	
115	  return {
116	    notifyAddedToWishlist: (productName: string) =>
117	      emitCartMessage(intl.formatMessage(messages.addedToWishlist, { productName }), 'success'),
118	    notifyAlreadyInWishlist: () => emitCartMessage(intl.formatMessage(messages.alreadyInWishlist), 'warning'),
119	    notifyMaxQuantityReached: () => emitCartMessage(intl.formatMessage(messages.maxQuantityReached), 'warning'),
120	  };
121	};

content.content:
514	#### Step 4.6 — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`: the real assembly (inserted 2026-09-20, built after 5.1 — see note)
515	
516	**Numbering note.** Labeled 4.6 because it's the piece B4 was always missing, not because it builds before B5's step 5.1 — it doesn't. It builds **last** among every B4/B5 content piece, because it needs all of them finished first: `cartItemMapper` (3.4), `useCartMergeAndCap` (4.2), `useCartMessages` (4.3), `ZimmCartItemActions` (4.4), `ZimmCartEmptyState` (4.5), and `ZimmCartButtonGroup` (5.1). Commit order (below) reflects this; the step numbering doesn't need to.
517	
518	**Why this step exists.** Found during step 4.2's own scoping (2026-09-19/20): `ZimmCartDrawer` (built commit 6) takes `children` as a prop and says so in its own docblock — *"the caller supplies the list... wired in a later commit in this same plan"* — but no step anywhere ever claimed that later commit. Same root cause as step 3.5's own insertion: a component built and tested in isolation, with its real integration point described in prose but never turned into an actual manifest line. `useCartMergeAndCap`'s own second call site (the "render guard," per its own step 4.2 text) has the same problem — no file was ever named for it. Both gaps share one fix: this container is the file that was missing.
519	
520	**Changes.** New file `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (+ `.test.tsx`) — already in B4's manifest (Tier 3, `@pwa-squad-a`), just never claimed by a step. `ProductItem` already has the `secondaryActions` prop slot built and wired (confirmed: `product-item/index.tsx:176,257,365`), so this step only fills it, it doesn't add it.
521	
522	**Correction, 2026-09-21, found while actually verifying this step's own pass criterion 5 against the real current code before dispatch — this step does NOT modify "nothing else."** `ZimmCartDrawer` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx:80`, built commit 6) has its own hardcoded ternary: `{itemCount === 0 ? <chakra.p>{EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT}</chakra.p> : children}` — it renders its own interim placeholder text and **ignores `children` entirely** whenever `itemCount === 0`. No matter what this container passes as `children` (a real item list, or `<ZimmCartEmptyState />`), the drawer will keep showing `EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT` at zero items, because that branch never reaches `children` at all. Pass criterion 5 ("Empty basket renders `ZimmCartEmptyState`, not an empty `children` array") is structurally unsatisfiable without also fixing this. Same shape of gap as this very step's own reason for existing (a component built with a documented placeholder, whose removal was implicitly assumed to be "a later commit" that no step ever actually claimed) — `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own docblock already says as much ("no real empty-state body... separate, later commits in this same plan").
523	
524	**Fix, now part of this step's own manifest:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/{index.tsx,index.test.tsx}` — remove the `itemCount === 0 ? ... : children` ternary and the now-dead `EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT` constant entirely; render `{children}` unconditionally. The empty-vs-populated decision moves entirely to this container, which is exactly the job it already exists to do. Same tier as every other file already in this step's scope (`ui-kits/organisms/`, Tier 3, `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b`) — not a multi-tier escalation. `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own existing test suite has an assertion keyed to the old hardcoded placeholder text at `itemCount === 0` that will need updating to assert whatever `children` was passed instead — a real, expected test update, not a regression.
525	
526	This container is the thing that:
527	1. Owns `useCurrentBasket()` — the one thing `components.md` forbids under `overrides/app/components/`, which is exactly why this lives under `overrides/app/pages/cart/` instead (open question 8's own resolution, finally acted on).
528	2. Maps each basket line through `cartItemMapper.ts` into `ProductItem` props, rendering the result as `ZimmCartDrawer`'s `children`.
529	
530	   **Clarified 2026-09-21, checked against the real current code before dispatch, not assumed:**
531	   `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own docblock already discloses that its output (`{itemId, productId,
532	   name, image, combinedAttributes, quantity, stepQuantity}`) is not what `ProductItem` actually
533	   consumes today — `ProductItem` takes a single `product: SfccProduct` prop (`SfccProduct = any`),
534	   which flows straight through `ItemVariantProvider` into `useItemVariant()`, and the leaves that
535	   read it (`item-price.tsx` in particular: `const { price, priceAfterItemDiscount } = variant`,
536	   plus `type.set`/`type.master`/`pricePerUnit`) need fields `cartItemMapper`'s output never
537	   included at all — it was never designed to be a complete `product` prop by itself. Base SFCC's
538	   own real precedent (`node_modules/.../product-item-list/index.jsx`, confirmed by reading it
539	   directly) builds this object as `{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[productItem.itemId]}` —
540	   the raw basket line item spread together with its matching full `Product` record (fetched via
541	   `useProducts({parameters: {ids: <comma-joined itemIds>}})` — **do NOT copy base's own
542	   `allImages: true`** on that call; over-fetching, and the exact parameter implicated in the
543	   SFCC-29 outage; this build needs one thumbnail per line, not every image). This container
544	   builds that same merged object per line and passes **that** as `ProductItem`'s `product` prop —
545	   `cartItemMapper.selectCartItemProps(...)`'s own output is still genuinely used "verbatim," just
546	   for what it's actually good for: supplying `productId`/`name` (as `productName`) to
547	   `ZimmCartItemActions` below, not as a substitute for the full merged object `ProductItem`
548	   itself needs. Do not invent a second, different image/attribute-selection algorithm for the
549	   merged object either — reuse `cartItemMapper`'s own `selectCartItemImage`/
550	   `selectCombinedAttributes` internals if `ProductItem`'s leaves need those exact values, rather
551	   than re-deriving them a second way. Base's bundle/bonus-product/multi-location-inventory
552	   handling in that same file is real complexity this epic's own manifest never asked for — do
553	   not replicate it; a plain per-line merge is sufficient scope here.
554	3. Calls `useCartMergeAndCap` as the render guard on every render — the second of its two call sites; the first (the post-auth callback) was already wired into `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` back in step 4.2 itself.
555	4. Supplies each item's `secondaryActions` with a real `ZimmCartItemActions`, wired to the actual remove/wishlist-move mutations — not a placeholder.
556	5. **Sequences the wishlist-move resume itself, so it never races the merge/cap correction (added 2026-09-20, Marcel's decision).** `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `onAuthSuccess` fires synchronously, before its merge call even starts — confirmed by reading the actual code during step 4.4's own build, not assumed — so a resume naively wired straight to that signal could act on a not-yet-merged, not-yet-capped basket. Deliberately **not** fixed by reordering `onAuthSuccess` itself: that signal has four other real consumers (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`, `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` itself) with no cart-merge dependency of their own, who want it to fire immediately for their own UX — changing its timing risks a real, unrelated regression to reach a guarantee only this container needs. Instead, this container's own resume handling must wait for the merge-then-cap chain it's already coordinating (item 3 above) to actually settle before invoking `onMoveToWishlist` for a resumed pending item (from step 4.4's `usePendingWishlistItem`) — the wait belongs here, in the one place that needs it, not in the shared hook everyone else also depends on.
557	
558	   **Mechanism, checked 2026-09-21 against `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s real current code, not
559	   invented — this hook exposes no "merge+cap settled" signal of its own, so this container needs
560	   its own independent one.** `onAuthSuccess` (line 177) fires before `mergeBasket.mutate(...)`
561	   (line 205) even starts, and the hook's return type has no other callback for this. What IS
562	   available: `capBasketQuantities` itself already resolves only once its own write (if any) has
563	   fully settled (its own JSDoc), and both the merge and the cap are React Query mutations, which
564	   `useIsMutating()` (the **reactive** hook — not `queryClient.isMutating()`, which is for an
565	   imperative point-in-time read, the opposite need here) tracks live across the whole app, since
566	   no basket mutation in this codebase carries a `mutationKey` to scope it. A workable approach:
567	   this container passes its own callback as `onAuthSuccess` (e.g. flipping a small piece of local
