630	## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)
631	
632	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
633	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
634	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
635	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
636	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
637	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
638	
639	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
640	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
641	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
642	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
643	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
644	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
645	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
646	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
647	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
648	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
649	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
650	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
651	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
652	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
653	3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
654	   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
655	   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
656	   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
657	   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
658	4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
659	   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
660	   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
661	   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
662	5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
663	   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
664	   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
665	   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
666	6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
667	   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
668	   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
669	   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
670	7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
671	   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
672	   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
673	   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
674	   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
675	8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
676	   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
677	   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
678	9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
679	   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
680	   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
681	   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
682	   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
683	   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
684	   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
685	   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
686	   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
687	   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
688	   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
689	   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
690	   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
691	   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about

#### Step 4.6 — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx`: the real assembly (inserted 2026-09-20, built after 5.1 — see note)

**Numbering note.** Labeled 4.6 because it's the piece B4 was always missing, not because it builds before B5's step 5.1 — it doesn't. It builds **last** among every B4/B5 content piece, because it needs all of them finished first: `cartItemMapper` (3.4), `useCartMergeAndCap` (4.2), `useCartMessages` (4.3), `ZimmCartItemActions` (4.4), `ZimmCartEmptyState` (4.5), and `ZimmCartButtonGroup` (5.1). Commit order (below) reflects this; the step numbering doesn't need to.

**Why this step exists.** Found during step 4.2's own scoping (2026-09-19/20): `ZimmCartDrawer` (built commit 6) takes `children` as a prop and says so in its own docblock — *"the caller supplies the list... wired in a later commit in this same plan"* — but no step anywhere ever claimed that later commit. Same root cause as step 3.5's own insertion: a component built and tested in isolation, with its real integration point described in prose but never turned into an actual manifest line. `useCartMergeAndCap`'s own second call site (the "render guard," per its own step 4.2 text) has the same problem — no file was ever named for it. Both gaps share one fix: this container is the file that was missing.

**Changes.** New file `overrides/app/pages/cart/cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (+ `.test.tsx`) — already in B4's manifest (Tier 3, `@pwa-squad-a`), just never claimed by a step. `ProductItem` already has the `secondaryActions` prop slot built and wired (confirmed: `product-item/index.tsx:176,257,365`), so this step only fills it, it doesn't add it.

**Correction, 2026-09-21, found while actually verifying this step's own pass criterion 5 against the real current code before dispatch — this step does NOT modify "nothing else."** `ZimmCartDrawer` (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/index.tsx:80`, built commit 6) has its own hardcoded ternary: `{itemCount === 0 ? <chakra.p>{EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT}</chakra.p> : children}` — it renders its own interim placeholder text and **ignores `children` entirely** whenever `itemCount === 0`. No matter what this container passes as `children` (a real item list, or `<ZimmCartEmptyState />`), the drawer will keep showing `EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT` at zero items, because that branch never reaches `children` at all. Pass criterion 5 ("Empty basket renders `ZimmCartEmptyState`, not an empty `children` array") is structurally unsatisfiable without also fixing this. Same shape of gap as this very step's own reason for existing (a component built with a documented placeholder, whose removal was implicitly assumed to be "a later commit" that no step ever actually claimed) — `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own docblock already says as much ("no real empty-state body... separate, later commits in this same plan").

**Fix, now part of this step's own manifest:** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmCartDrawer/{index.tsx,index.test.tsx}` — remove the `itemCount === 0 ? ... : children` ternary and the now-dead `EMPTY_BAG_PLACEHOLDER_TEXT` constant entirely; render `{children}` unconditionally. The empty-vs-populated decision moves entirely to this container, which is exactly the job it already exists to do. Same tier as every other file already in this step's scope (`ui-kits/organisms/`, Tier 3, `@pwa-squad-a @pwa-squad-b`) — not a multi-tier escalation. `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own existing test suite has an assertion keyed to the old hardcoded placeholder text at `itemCount === 0` that will need updating to assert whatever `children` was passed instead — a real, expected test update, not a regression.

This container is the thing that:
1. Owns `useCurrentBasket()` — the one thing `components.md` forbids under `overrides/app/components/`, which is exactly why this lives under `overrides/app/pages/cart/` instead (open question 8's own resolution, finally acted on).
2. Maps each basket line through `cartItemMapper.ts` into `ProductItem` props, rendering the result as `ZimmCartDrawer`'s `children`.

   **Clarified 2026-09-21, checked against the real current code before dispatch, not assumed:**
   `cartItemMapper.ts`'s own docblock already discloses that its output (`{itemId, productId,
   name, image, combinedAttributes, quantity, stepQuantity}`) is not what `ProductItem` actually
   consumes today — `ProductItem` takes a single `product: SfccProduct` prop (`SfccProduct = any`),
   which flows straight through `ItemVariantProvider` into `useItemVariant()`, and the leaves that
   read it (`item-price.tsx` in particular: `const { price, priceAfterItemDiscount } = variant`,
   plus `type.set`/`type.master`/`pricePerUnit`) need fields `cartItemMapper`'s output never
   included at all — it was never designed to be a complete `product` prop by itself. Base SFCC's
   own real precedent (`node_modules/.../product-item-list/index.jsx`, confirmed by reading it
   directly) builds this object as `{...productItem, ...productsByItemId[productItem.itemId]}` —
   the raw basket line item spread together with its matching full `Product` record (fetched via
   `useProducts({parameters: {ids: <comma-joined itemIds>}})` — **do NOT copy base's own
   `allImages: true`** on that call; over-fetching, and the exact parameter implicated in the
   SFCC-29 outage; this build needs one thumbnail per line, not every image). This container
   builds that same merged object per line and passes **that** as `ProductItem`'s `product` prop —
   `cartItemMapper.selectCartItemProps(...)`'s own output is still genuinely used "verbatim," just
   for what it's actually good for: supplying `productId`/`name` (as `productName`) to
   `ZimmCartItemActions` below, not as a substitute for the full merged object `ProductItem`
   itself needs. Do not invent a second, different image/attribute-selection algorithm for the
   merged object either — reuse `cartItemMapper`'s own `selectCartItemImage`/
   `selectCombinedAttributes` internals if `ProductItem`'s leaves need those exact values, rather
   than re-deriving them a second way. Base's bundle/bonus-product/multi-location-inventory
   handling in that same file is real complexity this epic's own manifest never asked for — do
   not replicate it; a plain per-line merge is sufficient scope here.
3. Calls `useCartMergeAndCap` as the render guard on every render — the second of its two call sites; the first (the post-auth callback) was already wired into `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts` back in step 4.2 itself.
4. Supplies each item's `secondaryActions` with a real `ZimmCartItemActions`, wired to the actual remove/wishlist-move mutations — not a placeholder.
5. **Sequences the wishlist-move resume itself, so it never races the merge/cap correction (added 2026-09-20, Marcel's decision).** `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `onAuthSuccess` fires synchronously, before its merge call even starts — confirmed by reading the actual code during step 4.4's own build, not assumed — so a resume naively wired straight to that signal could act on a not-yet-merged, not-yet-capped basket. Deliberately **not** fixed by reordering `onAuthSuccess` itself: that signal has four other real consumers (`header/rightBar`, `drawer-menu`, `product-view`, `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` itself) with no cart-merge dependency of their own, who want it to fire immediately for their own UX — changing its timing risks a real, unrelated regression to reach a guarantee only this container needs. Instead, this container's own resume handling must wait for the merge-then-cap chain it's already coordinating (item 3 above) to actually settle before invoking `onMoveToWishlist` for a resumed pending item (from step 4.4's `usePendingWishlistItem`) — the wait belongs here, in the one place that needs it, not in the shared hook everyone else also depends on.

   **Mechanism, checked 2026-09-21 against `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s real current code, not
   invented — this hook exposes no "merge+cap settled" signal of its own, so this container needs
   its own independent one.** `onAuthSuccess` (line 177) fires before `mergeBasket.mutate(...)`
   (line 205) even starts, and the hook's return type has no other callback for this. What IS
   available: `capBasketQuantities` itself already resolves only once its own write (if any) has
   fully settled (its own JSDoc), and both the merge and the cap are React Query mutations, which
   `useIsMutating()` (the **reactive** hook — not `queryClient.isMutating()`, which is for an
   imperative point-in-time read, the opposite need here) tracks live across the whole app, since
   no basket mutation in this codebase carries a `mutationKey` to scope it. A workable approach:
   this container passes its own callback as `onAuthSuccess` (e.g. flipping a small piece of local
   state), but does **not** treat the shopper as non-guest for `ZimmCartItemActions`' own `isGuest`
   prop purposes until `useIsMutating()` genuinely returns to `0` after that signal fires — since
   `onAuthSuccess` and the `mergeBasket.mutate(...)` call it precedes both run synchronously within
   the same effect body, the mutation is guaranteed to already be registered in the shared cache by
   the time this container's own re-render can observe it, so there is no window where the guard
   checks too early and finds nothing yet in flight. This is a starting hypothesis for the
   Implementer to build against and pressure-test — including the steady-state case where a
   shopper is already registered on mount, with nothing to wait for at all — not a settled design;
   verify it holds via pass criterion 4's own required controlled-timing proof rather than trusting
   real mutation timing to always land the same way in a test.
6. Calls `useCartMessages`'s three functions imperatively at the moments that actually need them (wishlist-move success, already-in-wishlist, max-quantity-reached) — **not** by passing anything into `ZimmCartDrawer`'s `messages` slot. **Corrected 2026-09-20, found by step 4.3's own Implementer:** that slot is `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own documented reservation for SFCC-404's future real message-aggregation system (see that component's own prop docblock, written back in step 1.2 — "Reserved slot for SFCC-404's message-aggregation system"), not for this interim toast. It couldn't be used for the toast anyway even setting that aside: a Chakra toast fired via `useToast()` is a fire-and-forget call into Chakra's own global toast portal, with no persistent "current" value a parent component could read back and render into a slot. Leave the `messages` slot passed as `undefined`/omitted by this container — the interim toast renders entirely independently of the drawer's own component tree.
7. Renders `ZimmCartEmptyState` in place of `children` when the basket has zero items.
8. Renders `ZimmCartButtonGroup` as `ZimmCartDrawer`'s `footer` slot.
9. Does **not** own `isOpen`/`onClose` itself — those arrive as props from whatever mounts this container (the final step, §9, via its own `useCartDrawer()` provider). This container's job is basket *content*, not the drawer's open/closed lifecycle — confirmed against `ZimmCartDrawer`'s own existing, unchanged prop contract (`isOpen`/`onClose` already required, already built).

**Also corrects §9's own text (see "B1 — revised file manifest" below):** that section currently says to mount `<ZimmCartDrawer />` directly in `_app`. Once this container exists, `_app` should mount `<CartDrawerContainer />` instead, which renders `<ZimmCartDrawer>` internally — otherwise the app repeats the exact gap already found in the base "AddToCartModal" precedent that section cites: `AddToCartModalProvider` is mounted in base `_app` today, but `<AddToCartModal />` itself is never rendered anywhere, base or override (confirmed by grepping the entire `retail-react-app` package) — so add-to-cart already shows no visual feedback in this app, and "mirroring" that pattern literally would just build the cart drawer the same non-functional way.

**Pass criteria.**
1. Renders one `ProductItem` per real basket line, using `cartItemMapper.ts`'s output verbatim — not a second, hand-rolled mapping.
2. `useCartMergeAndCap`'s render guard actually runs on a basket-driven re-render, and is proven (not assumed) to no-op while `useIsMutating()` is non-zero — this proves the wiring, step 4.2's own criterion 2 already proved the function. **Clarified 2026-09-20 (flagged by step 4.2's own Implementer, not yet a bug since this step hasn't been built):** "runs on a re-render" does not mean calling `capBasketQuantities` bare in the component's render body — that fires a side-effecting async function (it can issue a real mutation) during render, which React does not guarantee runs once, in order, or at all, and is a real correctness/purity violation, not just a style nit. Call it from `useEffect(() => { capBasketQuantities(basket); }, [basket])`, keyed on the basket state that actually changed — "runs on a basket-driven re-render" describes *when* the guard should trigger (whenever the basket's own relevant state changes), not *where in the render cycle* to place the call.
3. Each rendered item's `secondaryActions` is a real, wired `ZimmCartItemActions` — not a placeholder or omitted prop.
4. **A resumed wishlist-move genuinely waits for merge-then-cap to settle before firing (added 2026-09-20, see "Changes" item 5 above).** Prove this with a controlled-timing test — e.g. hold the merge/cap promise chain open with a manually-resolved promise, confirm `onMoveToWishlist` has not yet been called while it's pending, then resolve it and confirm the call happens after. An ordering that merely looks right when everything in a test resolves instantly (the same trap step 4.2's own callback-order criterion already named) does not satisfy this.
5. Empty basket renders `ZimmCartEmptyState`, not an empty `children` array. ## 5.0 Verification standard (added 2026-09-19, applies to every remaining step, 3.6 onward)

Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.

1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about
   whether it renders *at all*, and no other gate in this loop checks for it.

The reasoning that extraction isn't possible without touching `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx` (outside manifest) holds. 🟡 **should-fix, CONFIRMED (empirically, not guessed), ONE-OFF (only nested-drawer-in-drawer composition in this codebase today):** the code's own comment claims the fabricated-event focus degradation is "the same accepted degradation... Chakra falls back to focusing document.body." Kept at 🔵 not higher because extracting a shared hook requires touching `zimmWishlistAuthDrawer/index.tsx`, outside this step's manifest (Hard Rule 5) — correctly left alone, worth a follow-up ticket. 🔵 CONFIRMED / ONE-OFF, low stakes: `CartWishlistAuthGate`'s prop type is an inline anonymous object, not a named `CartWishlistAuthGateProps` per components.md convention — internal, non-exported, single-caller, single-field. ### 7. Yet "AC10" is cited as settled fact at `cartDrawerContainer.tsx:91`, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:87,135`, and `zimmDrawer/index.tsx:15-16,62`. Either a real Jira AC (project memory: ACs live in `customfield_10231`, not necessarily mirrored into these docs) that these build docs never captured, or a drifted citation propagated across 4 files.
